title: Small-batch PRs and risk mitigation notes
content:
Purpose:
Capture quick personal heuristics and a lightweight checklist for landing small, high-risk changes across the serving runtime. This is a scratchpad not a process doc; notes to self, half-baked ideas, and things to remember when I own the PR.

TL;DR:
- Prefer many small PRs (<= 200 LOC) for runtime bits that touch batching, kv-cache, or routing logic.
- For anything affecting token path or cache invalidation, include a deterministic smoke test and a rollback plan.
- Keep reviewers focused: annotate perf impacts and failure modes in the PR description.

Quick checklist (copy into PR desc):
- What changed and why (one short paragraph)
- Surface area: modules/files touched (list)
- Expected perf delta (p99 latency, throughput, memory) or N/A
- Safety flags: cache invalidation? backward-incompatible kv format? model-compat changes?
- Manual smoke steps (minimal): start local runtime, send 1-2 requests, check traces and kv hits
- Automated checks: unit tests added? integration test? end-to-end smoke? PR must not remove existing test coverage unless replaced
- Rollback instructions: which config to flip, tag to re-deploy, who to call

Risk mitigation patterns I keep reusing:
1) Feature flag + gradual rollout
   - Wrap risky refactor behind runtime flag (config-driven).
   - Canary with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% if green for 4 hours at each step.
   - Add metrics to monitor: kv-hit-rate, avg-token-latency, error-rate-by-route.

2) Safe migration for kv-cache changes
   - Dual-read mode: write new format while still reading old. Add migration job later.
   - If format change is needed, decouple via versioned keys and tombstones.

3) Local reproducibility
   - Make a minimal docker-compose or dev-run script so reviewers can reproduce flakiness locally. Keep it small and focused.

Refactor ideas to revisit (backlog):
- Extract small 'prefix-normalizer' util from router to remove repeated logic in 3 files. Should reduce bugs where prefix hashing mismatches.
- Replace ad-hoc retry logic in request_dispatch with a single RetryPolicy class and wire through the call graph.
- Move kv-cache eviction testing into deterministic unit harness that can simulate sequence of requests.

Follow-ups from recent PRs (notes to self):
- GH PR #4321: latency regression under long-seq workload. Need a perf test that simulates 2k tokens, and measure kernel selection path. Open item: add a 2k-token profile to the buildkite perf matrix.
- JIRA INF-987: customer reported cache-stale edge case when model pinned and routing fallback happened. Hypothesis: fallback path does not populate cache key version. Add assertion in fallback to write cache.

Lightweight experiments to run locally before the next PR:
- Microbench: run 1k iter of kv-get under contention with varying cache sizes to get a rough curve.
- Trace-level: instrument request id with a short tag showing router decision and kernel chosen; enable on dev cluster for an hour and sample.

Reviewer guidance (how I want feedback):
- Call out security/regression risks explicitly. If you spot a place where safe defaults are violated, add a blocking comment.
- Prefer small, actionable suggestions. If you think the change is larger, ask for a follow-up ticket instead of blocking the PR unless dangerous.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Decide on default rollout window for canary: 1 hour vs 4 hours? 1 hour catches fast regressions but might miss slow degradations.
- Should we enforce dual-read for all kv format changes via CI lint? Could be heavy.
- Add a shared checklist template in repo for runtime PRs. Might live as PR_TEMPLATE.md.

Notes to self (random):
- When debugging cache miss spike, check upstream load balancer spikes and also kernel OOMs. Often coincides with GC churn.
- Remind SRE to keep an eye when flipping flags for heavy routes (chat and embeddings routes are high QPS).

Quick links / artifacts to paste in PRs:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4321
- Jira: INF-987
- Slack thread: slack:#eng-serving-runtime ts=1432789123

End of scratchpad. Keep this short; prune stale items monthly.
